source.title: Distribution of Classification Margins: Are All Data Equal?
source.authors: Andrzej Banburski; Fernanda De La Torre; Nishka Pant; Ishana Shastri; T. Poggio

record.tranche_reason: The study measures margin distributions and their association with test performance, and tests removing training examples. These are different measures and interventions from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports margin and test-performance results, including natural versus randomized labels, but it does not report randomized-label held-out accuracy. Its removal experiments select examples by margin, not by memorization.
record.test_reason: The study tests margin-based predictors and compression by continuing training after removing high-margin examples. These do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or memorization-based removal. Its own random-label experiment establishes training-set separation, but does not establish the natural-versus-random held-out performance contrast required by V1. Optimizer and batch-size comparisons report compression penalties rather than the held-out comparisons specified in V4 and V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose margin-distribution AUC as an approximate ranking measure within an architecture and report substantial compression after full-data separation. They also emphasize that retained examples depend on initialization and emerge late, limiting the training speedup. Their strongest performance-preservation statements require qualification by the reported recipe-dependent losses.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures training-margin distributions and dynamically removes high-margin examples; it does not apply the interventions or measurements in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports margin flattening with both batch normalization and L2 regularization, and says flattening is not apparent without either. Compression outcomes vary with learning rate, batch size, optimizer, and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized-margin AUC and the proportion of small-margin examples predict test performance across different minima of a fixed architecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-margin distributions can rank generalization performance within a fixed architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Networks separate both natural and randomized training labels, but have larger normalized training margins with natural labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Successful training-set interpolation can coexist with substantially different normalized-margin distributions across label conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: After full-data training achieves separation, retaining only small-margin examples during further training can preserve much of the learned test performance; losses depend strongly on the compression recipe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin-based removal after separation can reduce the dataset needed for continued training, with recipe-dependent accuracy costs.

record.problems: The paper describes margin and test-error relationships largely through plots and qualitative trends, without reported uncertainty estimates. The natural-versus-random comparison reports training margins but not randomized-label held-out accuracy. Compression results depend on settings and include a separate DenseNet result with a larger reported performance decrease.
record.rows_left_out: No additional distinct result rows retained. Figure-only margin distributions over time and class-specific distributions are described qualitatively in Sections 4.3 and 4.2; they were not included because they do not test a listed version and add no separate quantified test-performance result.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting is demonstrated, but held-out accuracy for the paired random-label and natural-label models is not reported. The full coexistence contrast remains untested.
Compression penalties for Adam and SGD do not establish their relative held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions.
Compression penalties across batch sizes do not establish a large-batch generalization penalty under comparable fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation measure, correlation with generalization gaps, or comparison against alternative generalization measures.
No memorization-influence selection, equal-size random-removal control, or retraining from scratch after removal.

record.verdict_notes: No listed-version verdict is warranted. The paper's mention of chance performance for random labels is theoretical or attributed to prior work, rather than a reported held-out measurement in its own experiment. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not denials of the margin and compression findings.

versions.untested_parts: The paper compares margin distributions for natural and randomized labels, but does not report the randomized-label held-out accuracy needed to test coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization.
No width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison of held-out performance as stated in this version.
No large-batch generalization comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
The paper studies margin distributions, not magnitude-aware sharpness or weight perturbations scaled to weight magnitudes.
The paper removes examples selected by margin, not examples selected by memorization influence.

rows.subject: 100 conv nets (as in Section 3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared margin-distribution AUC with test error across networks initialized with varying standard deviation.
rows.measure: Association between margin-distribution AUC and test error
rows.value: The larger the margin AUC, the better the test performance.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a predictor for ranking minima of the same architecture.
rows.check: The association is between normalized-margin AUC and test error, not magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gap. Figure 2 averages AUC and test error within bins of ten networks.

rows.subject: 100 conv nets (as in Section 3)
rows.operation_detail: Grouped networks by number of small-margin datapoints and compared average test error.
rows.measure: Average test error by small-margin-data range
rows.value: Larger proportion of small margin data results in higher averages of test error.
rows.note: The figure caption also reports a margin-distribution cutoff of γ = 0.1 for the AUC plot.
rows.check: Counts of small-margin examples do not measure any listed version. The reported association with test error is accurately paraphrased.

rows.subject: Convolutional neural network trained with natural labels
rows.stage_stated: after data separation and close to margin convergence
rows.operation_detail: Compared the training-set margin distribution with that of a network trained on randomized labels.
rows.value: Margins for all datapoints are larger for natural labels than for randomized labels.
rows.note: This is a margin comparison, not a report of held-out accuracy for the randomized-label network.
rows.check: The natural-label training-margin distribution does not establish the held-out contrast in V1. Positive training margins establish separation only.

rows.subject: Convolutional neural network trained with randomized labels
rows.stage_stated: after data separation and close to margin convergence
rows.operation_detail: Compared the distribution of the 100 smallest training margins with the natural-label network.
rows.measure: Counts across ten bins of the smallest-margin range
rows.value: The first five bins had more datapoints than for natural labels; the first bin had 14 versus one.
rows.note: The reported comparison concerns training margins, not held-out performance.
rows.check: The bin counts concern training margins, not randomized-label held-out accuracy. The supplementary experiment explicitly confirms zero random-label training error, but does not supply the missing held-out comparison.

rows.subject: Convolutional network (CIFAR10) with SGD
rows.operation_detail: Removed datapoints with the largest margins, retaining 200 training datapoints.
rows.baseline: network trained on the full dataset
rows.note: The reported result is for margin-selected data removal, not removal of memorized examples.
rows.check: The 2.89% accuracy reduction concerns continued training after margin-based removal, not retraining from scratch after memorization-based removal. The baseline should specify continued full-dataset training; the network had already learned from all 50,000 examples.

rows.subject: DenseNet-BC (CIFAR10)
rows.operation_detail: Compressed the training set to 200 datapoints selected by margin.
rows.baseline: network trained on the full dataset
rows.note: Table 1 reports drop in test performance after compression; the paper also describes a separate DenseNet experiment with a 4.49% decrease.
rows.check: The 0.11% result additionally requires batch size 50. It is a compression penalty after full-data training, not evidence for V8. Correct the architecture description to block configuration 6, 12, 12, 16. The separate 4.49% DenseNet result uses a different compression setting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
